symptom: The standalone untrusted cross-envelope replay checker validated each batch element, then retained references to the caller's original mutable freeze and settlement revision objects. A later array index descriptor Proxy could rewrite the earlier cohort or revision digest after that earlier envelope was admitted. The replay map then compared two later matching values and missed a conflicting receipt or source revision identity; no independent authority or scoring was granted.
lesson: A replay index that stores references to caller-owned envelope objects is not stable, even when each envelope passed strict structural validation. Later batch traversal can change the earlier map entry and hide cross-envelope conflicts.
guardrail: Copy the entire bounded, strict own-data-descriptor batch into a detached graph before per-envelope semantic validation and replay map construction. Never retain original caller references in receipt or revision indexes. Assert that later array descriptor mutations actually execute and cannot hide either a cohort receipt collision or a revision-content collision. Preserve literal deny-only authority flags.
